quote:
Landowner participation and commitment is essential at all stages of any restoration 
programme. Wherever possible, reforestation plans should be integrated into 
community development and resource management plans. Any changes to the plans 
must be discussed and agreed by all the stakeholders, who should be made aware 
of the requirements needed for the project and expectations for contributions from all 
involved.

quote:
The single most important factor in designing a suc-
cessful mangrove restoration project is determining the
normal hydrology (depth, duration and frequency, and
of tidal ﬂooding) of existing natural mangrove plant
communities (a reference site) in the area in which you
wish to do restoration.

model_use.method: expert restoration-design recommendation; use local natural reference hydrology

reported_values.source_importance: single most important factor applies to the combined depth-duration-frequency hydrology group, not a numeric weight on duration

context.numeric_calibration: No executable global hydroperiod function. The abstract generalisation and site curves are retained for review with counterexamples; duration and frequency are not interchangeable. Local tidal datum, drainage and reference-system transfer remain unresolved.
context.applicability_hold: General reference-site method only; no Florida/Australia elevations or percentages transferred globally.

quote:
Secondary succession depends
upon mangrove propagule availability, and I suggest
a new term, “propagule limitation” to describe situa-
tions in which mangrove propagules may be limited
in natural availability due to removal of mangroves by
development, or hydrologic restrictions or blockages
(i.e. dikes) which prevent natural waterborne transport
of mangrove propagules to a restoration site.

context.applicability_hold: Natural recovery pathway only. Planting can address propagule limitation; not a hard exclusion for the whole tidal-coastal family.
